core_dependencies.description: Entry point invokes the CLI dispatch layer to run the application.
CLI dispatches parsed commands to command handlers.
Handlers use the Storage class to persist Task records.
Handlers construct and manipulate Task domain models.
Storage obtains SQLite connections via core connect() factory.
Sync service reads local tasks and pushes them to remote storage.
Reminder mail uses slugify for naming identifiers.
Report rendering queries tasks via the shared DB connection factory.
Storage writes rows into the tasks table defined by schema.sql; no code-level reference, only shared schema contract.
Root manifest declares the main.py → cli.py → handlers.py dependency chain.

key_insights: Clean layered architecture: execution flows downward from main.py → cli.py → handlers.py → storage.py → core/db.py, with no upward dependencies.
src/core is the shared foundation: both storage.py and the services layer depend on its connect() and slugify() primitives, making it the highest fan-in module.
db/schema.sql is a pure data contract — the tasks table schema couples the database to storage.py without any import-level dependency, so schema drift is a risk if not versioned alongside code.

The services layer sits parallel to handlers.py rather than being called by it; if handlers never invoke services, features like sync and reminders may only be reachable through a separate entry path — worth verifying wiring.
No circular dependencies are evident; the only declared-graph file (handwritten.claims.json) confirms a linear entry chain.
models.py is a leaf dependency used by both handlers and storage, which is healthy — but services may bypass it if they query raw SQL directly via core/db.
